sections.title: 13. Agent Harness playbook (state machine · action protocol · async · artifacts · contracts)
sections.summary: Succeeds chapters 2/4/5/6/7/8/9 from before AGENTS.md was condensed: the two-layer state machine and its two mandatory gates, the action protocol and the three `--drive` modes, the async inbox and the cross-process closeout, progress views, run artifacts, the Mod-change trio, and the host contract. Mechanics are looked up on the spot (guide.show harness) and never restated in AGENTS.md.

rules.text: goal authorization is a **run-level self-declared record**: `config.set goal.authorization=<one-line note>` writes `settings.goal.authorization` (trimmed, ≤ 200 characters, no newline; an empty value clears it explicitly). Only runs that entered goal **at runtime** (`settings.play.mode=goal`) are checked before `review.note` closes: a missing record blocks with a narrative line, writes no `ending` and does not advance; a static `goal` preset in `data/config.json` is the repository owner's standing configuration and is **out of scope** (otherwise the all-1 smoke walk would break). Switching back to guide is not checked, and resume keeps the record. The record only proves "a sentence was registered", not that the user said it — never claim it as identity proof, and it never enters `agent.summary`.
rules.basis: user decision 2026-11-01 (E2 ruling: the closing check covers runtime goal only; a static default does not block)

rules.text: The coordinator is a **live self-loop** — the kernel FSM has exactly one true transition, `live → retired` (R1): the run opens in the charter act (`run.phase=="charter"`, charter trio via `charter.set`) → `run.begin` opens the standing coordinate act (`run.phase==""`, self-loop: dispatch / serial acceptance / both gates / conflicts) → `coordinate.submit` (queue drained) enters the settle act (`run.phase=="settle"`, four items linearly: `verify.submit` → `settlement.evolution` → `settlement.sessions` → `settlement.todo`) → four items complete auto-advances to the release act (`run.phase=="release"`, R9 effect, no event spent) → `release.confirm` / `release.skip` declare the batch's develop→master outcome → `review.note` settles the batch (`run.phase=""`, `run.batch+1`, back to coordinate) or, with `run.retire` armed, stamps the one true transition to `retired`. `verify.submit=false` sends the whole batch back to coordinate (settlement and release keys cleared).

There is one requirement pipeline per requirement. Stored truth is exactly **2 states** (`req.<i>.status`): `open` / `done` — everything else is derived, never stored; `split` / `merged` / `dropped` are values of the `closed_reason` field (R11), not states. Inside `open` the requirement walks nine micro-states derived by the single-source judge `req_phase()` (menus / render / beats legend all read it — no second copy anywhere): draft(立项) → planning(计划中) ──proposal.submit(plan)──▶ plan_gate(计划门禁) ──gate.approve──▶ ready(待开发) ──requirement.dispatch(+lane)──▶ developing(开发中) ──proposal.submit(development)──▶ dev_review(交付受理) ──proposal.accept──▶ accept_gate(验收门禁) ──gate.approve──▶ integrating(集成) ──integration.confirm──▶ done(完成, terminal). Three push-back paths (`proposal.reject` on a development delivery / `gate.reject` on the accept gate / `integration.reject`) land uniformly in ready (R6: `plan_ok` kept, `job=""`, lane released); `gate.reject` on the plan gate returns to planning with `plan_ok=false`. The two overlay markers (`blocked` / `stale`) stack on top of the phase display and are not states; `analyzing` survives only as a legacy-save compatibility value.

The old side states are demoted (D-MA23): `split` / `merged` / `dropped` are now values of the `closed_reason` field on a closed (`done`) row (R11 — a closed reason, not a state); the two marker overlays stay display-only: `blocked` (unresolved conflict or needs_amend, cleared by `requirement.resolve` / `requirement.amend`) and `stale` (a proposal whose rev is outdated, cleared automatically once a rebase proposal lands).

The coordinator does exactly four things — dispatch (requirement.dispatch), accept proposals serially (proposal.accept / proposal.reject), pass the two mandatory gates (gate.approve / gate.reject), and walk each batch boundary (coordinate.submit → the settle act's four items → release.confirm / release.skip → review.note batch settle or retire); it never carries development itself — the feature→develop integration of a requirement belongs to its development executor (`integration.confirm` / `integration.reject`) — and it may never bypass a gate.

Requirement granularity: adjacent work with the same goal, the same subsystem, a small change, or that can share one plan and one acceptance evidence set belongs in the same requirement; create a new one only for an independent delivery + acceptance, a cross-repository or cross-lane change, or risk isolation. A new adjacent requirement must state in its description why it cannot be merged (no reason = treat as mergeable). Three-question criterion: ① the blocked action is filing through requirement.add / --requirement; ② the visible symptom of a violation is that the adjacent requirement is pointed out as "just part of the previous one" while its description has no cannot-merge reason; ③ confirm it next time by walking `requirement.list` and checking that every new requirement's description carries that reason.

The plan gate (`req.gate=plan`) fires when a plan proposal is submitted (D-MA23: gate-on-submit — the plan side has no proposal.accept hop); approve → `plan_ok=true` (the ready act, the only phase that may dispatch into development; the reactive auto-dispatch may continue into developing in the same turn); reject → back to planning with `plan_ok=false`, `rev+1` and the feedback written; it validates `gate_rev == req.rev` (otherwise stale, approval is not allowed).

The accept gate (`req.gate=accept`) fires after the main agent accepts the development proposal (the executor delivered); approve → the integrating act (`integrating=true`, gate cleared) — done is NOT granted here, the executor still has to land `integration.confirm` with `develop@<sha>` evidence; reject → the ready act (`plan_ok` keeps its value: not amended → back into the development queue; amended → `plan_ok` was already invalidated → planning, must be replanned); it validates `gate_rev == req.rev` and requires non-empty `artifacts` — a summary-only completion claim is not accepted.
accept means the executor self-checked and delivered; it does not mean the main agent has accepted. Only gate.approve is the verification.

A requirement sitting on the plan / accept gate (`req.gate ~= ""`) cannot be dispatched, accepts no new proposal and cannot be skipped; even automatic advancement (`--drive cmd:…`) runs one `gate.approve` per gate — only the index comes from the external decision command.
